ĐANG HỌC
Hello and welcome to English with Anna, the podcast where we talk about life, learning, and the English language.
#2
I'm your host, Anna, and today we have a very special guest.
#3
Please welcome David.
#4
Hi, Anna.
#5
Thank you so much for inviting me.
#6
I'm excited to be here.
#7
It's a pleasure, David.
#8
Today's topic is simple but very close to the heart.
#9
We are going to talk about my country.
#10
This topic is very useful for English learners.
#11
So David, are you ready?
#12
Absolutely.
#13
Let's begin.
#14
So David, can you tell us which country you are from?
#15
Sure.
#16
I'm from the United States of America.
#17
It's a big country in North America.
#18
My country is known for its diversity, technology, and fast lifestyle.
#19
There are 50 states and I live in New York.
#20
Oh, that's wonderful.
#21
I've heard a lot about New York.
#22
Is it true that it's called the city that never sleeps?
#23
Yes, that's right.
#24
New York City is always awake.
#25
You can find people working, eating, and walking even at midnight.
#26
It's very exciting.
#27
That sounds amazing.
#28
What do you love most about your country?
#29
Well, there are many things I love about my country.
#30
But I think the best thing is the freedom we have.
#31
People are free to speak, follow any religion, and choose any career.
#32
I also love the natural beauty.
#33
We have mountains, forests, beaches, and deserts.
#34
That's great.
#35
Freedom is really important.
#36
David, can you describe your flag for our listeners?
#37
Sure.
#38
The American flag has 13 red and white stripes and 50 white stars on a blue background.
#39
The stripes represent the original 13 colonies and the stars represent the 50 states.
#40
It's a symbol of unity and pride.
#41
That's a good explanation.
#42
Now, let me share about my country.
#43
I am from the United Kingdom.
#44
It's in Europe and includes England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
#45
Oh, yes.
#46
The UK is a beautiful country.
#47
I've always wanted to visit London.
#48
You should.
#49
London is wonderful.
#50
We have the famous Big Ben, the London Eye, and Buckingham Palace.
#51
The history and culture of the UK are very rich.
#52
We are also known for our literature like Shakespeare and Jane Austin.
#53
That's really interesting.
#54
What do you love most about your country?
#55
I love the calm countryside, the traditions, and our sense of humor.
#56
And of course, I enjoy our tea culture.
#57
Most British people love to have a cup of tea every day.
#58
Haha, I've heard about that.
#59
Tea time sounds lovely.
#60
Yes, it is.
#61
So, David, what are some festivals celebrated in your country?
#62
Oh, we celebrate many festivals.
#63
The biggest one is probably Thanksgiving.
#64
It's a day to thank for the harvest and blessings.
#65
Families get together and eat a big meal, usually with turkey, mashed potatoes, and pumpkin pie.
#66
We also celebrate Independence Day on July 4th, with fireworks.
#67
I've seen pictures of that.
#68
It looks like a lot of fun.
#69
In the UK, we celebrate Christmas, Easter, and also Guyox night with fireworks.
#70
It's a day to remember a historical event.
#71
That's interesting.
#72
What language do most people speak in your country?
#73
English is the main language, but we also have Welsh, Scots, Gaelic, and Irish in different parts.
#74
And in your country, English is the main language, too.
#75
But we have people from all over the world.
#76
So, you'll hear Spanish, Chinese, Arabic, and many more languages.
#77
It's very multicultural.
#78
That makes your country very colorful.
#79
Let's talk about the education system.
#80
Can you tell us how schools work in the USA?
#81
Sure.
#82
We have elementary school from age 5 to 11, middle school from 11 to 14 and high school from 14 to 1818.
#83
After that, students can go to college or university.
#84
Education is very important in our society.
#85
It's similar in the UK.
#86
We also have primary, secondary, and then further education.
#87
Now, let's talk about food.
#88
What is your favorite food from your country?
#89
That's a tough one.
#90
I love hamburgers, hot dogs, and apple pie.
#91
But we also have dishes from all over the world like tacos, sushi, and pasta.
#92
What about you, Anna?
#93
I love our traditional roast dinner.
#94
It usually includes roasted meat, potatoes, and vegetables with gravy.
#95
And of course, fish and chips is a classic.
#96
Sounds delicious.
#97
I really want to try that.
#98
You must.
#99
So, David, what message would you give to English learners who want to talk about their country?
#100
I would say keep it simple.
#101
Talk about the name of your country, where it is, what language people speak, what festivals are celebrated, and what food you like.
#102
Share what makes you proud.
#103
Don't worry about grammar.
#104
Just express yourself.
#105
That's great advice.
#106
And I would add, listen to podcasts like this, learn new words, and try speaking every day.
#107
Your country is part of your identity, and it's a great topic to practice English.
#108
Well said, Anna.
#109
Thank you, David, for joining us today.
#110
It was a pleasure talking with you.
#111
Thank you for having me.
#112
I really enjoyed it.
#113
And thank you to all our listeners for spending time with us today.
#114
We hope this conversation helps you build confidence to speak about your own country in English.
#115
If you liked this episode, please give it a thumbs up, leave a comment, and share it with your friends who are also learning English.
#116
Don't forget to subscribe to Everyday English with Anna.
#117
so you never miss an episode.
#118
Keep practicing, stay curious, and remember,
#119
every day is a chance to learn something new.
#120
Until next time, take care and keep speaking English.
👀
